This game tries to combine modern Assassin's Creed RPGs with old school parkour stealth games and does that pretty well. The RPG part is toned down a lot but imo it still allows for flexibility and different playstyles. Instead of just getting a ton of XP for every move your main side activity reward is one of three different types of coins, which you can use for different things, such as opening special chests or bribing soldiers. This feels really gamey but it helps you focus your playstyle towards getting the rewards you want, instead of just being overwhelmed by all kinds of boring activities and procedurally generated sidequests like in the previous games. It also helps the game feel much less bloated. Also, Baghdad is beautiful and the game is worth playing just to explore it.

Cons : Small Map, Not playable without map pack as guards are going to bunt you down before you figure out where the nearest posters are. This wasn't a problem in other games because protagonists were stronger and had more stamina. Bassim just can't dodge attacks if his stamina goes down. But bassim can also scale great heights which requires stamina, so it stupid whe he loses his stamina when he does a rolling dodge. (You can parry infinitely but every second attack is unblockable). So need adjustments in gameplay. I think more frequent attacks with less unblockable attacks plus lower stamina cost for dodging will fix this.

I really enjoyed Assassin’s Creed Mirage. It brings back that classic stealth-focused gameplay and the setting in Baghdad is beautifully done. The architecture and environmental detail are amazing—it feels like ancient Iraq, pristine and vibrant. Missions can be a bit one-dimensional at times, and less intriguing than earlier games.

The story is solid and well-paced, showing Basim before the events of Valhalla, but it’s heavily tied to Valhalla’s ending—so if you haven’t played that, parts of the story won’t land. Honestly feels more like a narrative DLC than a full standalone title.

Assassin’s Creed™ Mirage delivers on its promise to return to the franchise’s roots—and for me, it absolutely succeeds. The classic stealth gameplay is back with instant assassinations that feel satisfyingly familiar. While the RPG elements in titles like Origins added a layer of complexity, they often made stealth feel more like a numbers game than a test of strategy. Mirage strips that back, and in doing so, brings the fun and fluidity back to sneaking through crowds and taking out targets.

The simplified weapon system—with fewer weapons and more straightforward scaling—helps avoid the bloat that crept into recent entries. And then there’s Baghdad: beautifully rendered, vibrant, and incredibly easy to navigate. The city itself becomes a playground for stealth, exploration, and parkour. All in all, Mirage feels like a refreshing return to form for the series—a focused, stylish, and thoroughly enjoyable Assassin’s Creed experience.
